sentences.text: The only known species of this dinosaur is Analong chuanjieensis.
In 2008, an exhibition called Lufeng World Dinosaur Valley was constructed around the skeletons.
Two giant sauropod skeletons were discovered in 1995 by Tao Wang while working with the Lufeng Dinosaur Museum in the village of A'na and the town of Chuanjie in Lufeng County, Yunnan.
The skeletons remained in situ until 2000, when they were described and named Chuanjiesaurus.

In 2020, Xin-Xin Ren and colleagues re-examined the specimen LFGT LCD9701-1 and determined that it was distinct enough from the Chuanjiesaurus holotype to warrant a new genus and species, Analong chuanjiensis.

The genus name Analong refers to the village of A'na and the suffix '-long' means 'dragon' in Mandarin, while the specific epithet chuanjieensis refers to the town of Chuanjie where the fossils were found.
Ren and colleagues originally classified Analong as a basally-branching member of Mamenchisauridae, and subsequent studies have reaffirmed Analong's classification as a mamenchisaurid.
Analong lived between 170.9 and 168.2 million years ago during the Bajocian age.
